articleTitle: Output Feedback Control for High-Order Nonlinear Systems With Practical Predefined-Time Convergence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: The practical predefined-time (PPT) output feedback control issue of higher-order nonlinear systems is investigated in this paper. First, a state observer was designed to ensure the observer error to be PPT stable via the time-varying function method. Then, with the derived observer, a PPT output feedback controller is derived. Through the Lyapunov technique, it is demonstrated that the tracking error can reach a small region around zero in predefined time with unavailability of full-state measurements. Finally, the performance of the proposed controller is shown by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Diagnosability of the Lexicographic Product of Paths and Paths under PMC Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: In a multiprocessor system, if the number of faulty processors is less than t, and the system can identify all faulty processors directly without any exchanging, then the system’s diagnosability is t. The multiprocessor system’s interconnection network plays a crucial role in determining it’s diagnosability. Evaluating the diagnosability of multiprocessor systems necessitates a comprehensive analysis of their interconnection networks. As the size of multiprocessor systems’ interconnection networks continues to increase, any processor failures or physical connection failures can significantly impact the systems’ stability and efficiency. This paper focuses on studying the networks obtained by lexicographic product of paths and paths, and obtains its diagnosability as well as its h-edge tolerable diagnosability under the PMC model.

articleTitle: Analysis of Three-Body Pitching Motion of New Unmanned Boat Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: When the current rescue unmanned boat is sailing on the sea, the vertical shake on the boat is too large, which will lead to a great reduction in the sailing performance of rescue unmanned boats. This article uses the three-body boat modal water vertical shake attenuation experiments as the research object. The programming ideas based on systematic identification methods and genetic algorithms, and establish four vertical system identification mathematical models. Through experiments, the peak of the boat model increased, the peak of the vertical corner speed increased, and the time of the boat model reached a stable state increase. Secondly, the best fitting model pitch motion identification equation is obtained, which not only verifies the feasibility of the unmanned vehicle model, but also verifies the reliability of the adapted software. Finally, through the comparison of dual - boating models, the three-body boat models have a good reduction effect.

articleTitle: Research on Load Transfer Law of Artillery Equipment under Complex Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: This article focuses on the problem of load transfer during artillery firing under different soil boundary conditions, considering the complex boundary coupling effect and the law of system load transfer and boundary influence. On the basis of traditional dynamic simulation methods, a combination of spatial springs and damping friction is used to simulate the deformation behavior of soil. This system is used to establish equivalent displacement conditions for soil boundaries. Subsequently, efficient and high-precision dynamic modeling research was conducted on artillery. The parameter values of the boundary combination model are determined by solving the fitting test data through dynamic simulation, forming a soil boundary submodel. A large caliber self-propelled gun is tested and compared with the high-speed camera monitoring results of the vehicle displacement, parking hoe displacement, and hydraulic oil pressure monitoring results of the parking hoe during the shooting test. The simulation results meet the accuracy requirements. Compared with the traditional multi-body dynamics model, this method has higher simulation accuracy and does not increase the simulation complexity and computational scale, which can be applied to the development of the same type of artillery equipment to improve the simulation and design efficiency in the process of artillery equipment development.

articleTitle: Modeling and Data Analysis of Strip Steel Edge Tracking Efficiency Based on ABAQUS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: In order to address the issue of low control efficiency in strip steel edge tracking during precision rolling, this study developed a dynamic coupling finite element model of the rolling mill rolls and the strip using the ABAQUS software. The aim is to investigate the functional relationship between the roll gap tilt and the strip steel edge deviation at the exit. The research primarily analyzes the influence of strip width, strip thickness, and steel grade on strip steel edge deviation, and under different roll gap tilt conditions, it outputs the variation in deviation and obtains the control coefficient for strip steel edge tracking through interpolation fitting. The results indicate that the influence of steel grade on control efficiency is significantly higher than that of width and thickness, with width being secondary and thickness having the smallest impact. Through interpolating the data, the control coefficient for strip steel edge tracking can be obtained under different operating conditions, higher control efficiency is achieved with a greater roll gap tilt and a smaller control coefficient. This study provides a theoretical foundation for the control of strip steel edge tracking in industrial precision rolling processes.

articleTitle: Data Analysis on the Impact of Internal Defects on the Torsional Resistance of Thin-walled Cylinders
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Thin-walled cylinder structures feature widely in aerospace, energy transmission, and other fields. The existence of internal defects therein will gravely influence structural mechanical properties and safety. This study established finite element models of thin-walled cylinders with and without internal defects, and numerically simulated stress and deformation distributions of the two models under torsional loading. Results revealed internal defects exerted minimal impact on models under small loading; whereas loading amplified sufficiently, stresses and deformations proximate to defect regions would sharply rise, with maximum stress reaching 150 MPa and maximum deformation 1.687 mm. This provides potential for detecting internal defects by differences between stress variables and theoretical values. Study conclusions indicate effective detection of internal defects in thin-walled cylinders necessitates external loading induces extensive metal plastic flow. This study provides a theoretical foundation for enhancing safety in such structures.

articleTitle: Research on Stress Prediction Model of Steel Plate Leveling Based on FEM and PSO-BP
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Leveling is an indispensable process in steel plate production, and the quality of leveling directly affects the quality of steel plate production. The leveling quality has many links with the dynamic changes of steel plates in the leveling process. In this paper, by combining the particle swarm optimization-backpropagation neural network (PSO-BP) with the finite element method (FEM), a surrogate model of the leveling parameters and the state of the steel plate during leveling was constructed, which can calculate the information of the steel plate in the leveling process in real-time, and verify the model’s accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on the Assessment Method of Lower Limb Muscle Fatigue Based on Surface Electromyography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Muscle fatigue frequently occurs in the rehabilitation process of patients. In recent years, time-domain parameters, frequency-domain parameters, and nonlinear methods have been widely applied in muscle fatigue assessment. This study introduces a new muscle fatigue assessment index: the Area Ratio Modification Index (ARMI). We compared it with seven common assessment indices - Mean Absolute Value (MAV), Root Mean Square (RMS), Integrated EMG (IEMG), Mean Power Frequency (MPF), Median Frequency (MF), Permutation Entropy (PE), and Approximate Entropy (ApEn). Ten healthy volunteers participated in muscle fatigue experiments involving isometric and isotonic contractions. The experimental results showed that as muscle fatigue intensified, the values of MAV, RMS, IEMG, and ARMI in the sEMG signals exhibited an increasing trend, while the values of MPF, MF, ApEn, and PE showed a decreasing trend. By comparing the change rates (CR) of these seven indicators before and after fatigue, it was found that the CR of ARMI was higher than the other seven indicators. Therefore, this study demonstrates that ARMI is an effective and sensitive muscle fatigue assessment index, offering higher sensitivity and effectiveness compared to the other seven indices.

articleTitle: Single and Multiple Holes Image Visualization of Aluminum Surface Detected by Laser Ultrasonic Wave Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: This study introduces a method for visualizing holes automatically utilizing ultrasonic wavefield pictures acquired by a noncontact laser scanning device. Hidden holes and leaks exist extensively in material structures in the industries, such as defense, aerospace, electrical power, oil and gas, and transportation, which affect the public safety and reliability seriously. Therefore, it is of great need to detect and monitor holes and leakage in materials. In this paper, based on the theory of laser ultrasound, an automatic laser scanner detection system (Lamb wave) was designed and developed. The laser scanning experiments were carried out on aluminum plates having holes through this system and the relationship among the laser wave energy, two-waves mixing interferometer TWMI and holes or leakage was analyzed. The visualization of the damaged area was achieved through the application of ultrasonic laser wave scanning principles. The efficacy of the suggested laser ultrasonic scanning equipment and imaging processing technique is confirmed through experimental validation using laser ultrasonic scanning images acquired from an aluminum plate. The results unequivocally demonstrated the successful detection and visualization of concealed and imperceptible openings or leaks on the scanned surface. In conclusion, the proposed method enables rapid detection and evaluation of defects, with the detection results being visualized. This highlights its great potential for market application in industries requiring efficient hole and leakage detection, addressing concerns related to public safety and reliability.

articleTitle: Flatness Measurement of Steel Strip Using Three Laser Stripes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of machine vision technology, flatness measurement devices based on line-structured light have been gradually applied to strip steel production lines. However, in the complex and harsh environments of industrial sites, the vibration and rotation of the strip can impact the results of flatness measurement, leading to measurement errors. This paper proposes a flatness measurement device based on triple-line light sources to address this challenge. The device uses an industrial camera to capture the projection of three lasers on the surface of the strip. By repeatedly collecting data from the same position on the steel strip, it achieves high-precision measurement of strip flatness. We designed simulated experiments. The results indicate that the proposed method effectively eliminates measurement errors caused by steel strip vibration and rotation, thereby improving flatness measurement accuracy. This approach has certain reference value for the improvement of flatness measurement technology in industrial environments.

articleTitle: Development and Application of a Model for Cold Strip Rolling Human Operating Frequency Determination and Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Enhancing the unit's automation to achieve fully automatic rolling has become the current urgent challenge in cold rolling. In accordance with these requirements, automatic determination of human intervention in cold strip rolling was achieved by monitoring operational items. The results demonstrated that this monitoring method achieved an accuracy rate of over 99%. Additionally, a cold strip rolling evaluation model was established using a combination of the Combined Weighting (CW) method and the technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) algorithm. The evaluation results provide a direction for further improving the automation level of steel rolling. Furthermore, statistics on the automatic rate of operational items for each cold rolling equipment were compiled based on the level of human intervention. The changing patterns of each operational item's automatic rate over time were identified, along with areas requiring improvement. The industrial application of this approach provides evaluation indices and data support for minimizing human intervention in the rolling process, thereby significantly contributing to achieving fully automatic cold rolling.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Residual Stress Fields on Workpiece Surface Using Surrogate Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: The knowledge of the distribution of residual stress fields on mechanical component surfaces holds significant implications for ensuring dimensional stability of workpieces and mitigating fatigue crack initiation. To address the limitations of current detection methods in capturing continuous stress fields, the bivariate high-order polynomial surrogate model incorporating L2 regularization terms was proposed to characterize stress components. The reconstruction analysis of surface stress fields was conducted by measuring a set of discrete sampling points as initial values. Analyses of two discrete experimental datasets were used to demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in accurately approximating stress values, while maintaining robust generalization capabilities. The influence of sampling point position on reconstruction accuracy was analyzed by reducing the dataset size, providing a novel proposal for surface stress field reconstruction and sampling point selection.

articleTitle: LSTM-based modeling of the Tangnaihai and Fen River basins Rainfall Runoff Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: In this study, the Tangnaihai basin, characterized by weak human activities at the source of the Yellow River, and the Fenhe River basin, marked by significant human activities in the middle reaches of the Yellow River, were chosen as research subjects. Rainfall and runoff simulations with forecasting foresight periods of 1-3 days were conducted using LSTM and BPNN models. Despite declining simulation accuracy with longer forecast periods, LSTM consistently outperforms BPNN. Notably, the LSTM model effectively captures the hydrological nuances of different watershed types, although the precise internal hidden layer structure and historical information inputs remain ambiguous. The study reveals that watersheds experiencing strong human disturbances necessitate a complex hidden layer structure for accurate rainfall and runoff simulation. Furthermore, it is observed that the model’s dependence on historical information diminishes with the extension of the forecast period, highlighting the evolving relationship between historical data and forecasting accuracy.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Internal Defect Detection in Aluminum Alloy Pipes Aims to Provid Data Support for AI Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: The online effective detection of internal defects in metals has long faced many challenges. The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has provided possibilities for improving defect detection techniques. However, AI algorithms rely heavily on large amounts of data, which are difficult to obtain through traditional experimental methods. To address this issue, this study proposes a method for the internal defect detection of aluminum alloy pipes and provides data support for AI models and algorithms. We established a "pinch roller-pressure roller-aluminum alloy pipes" model and obtained the variation rules of Mises stress, constraint reaction force caused by the change of internal defect position through numerical calculation. The results show that the position change of the internal defect has a clear functional relationship with the constraint reaction force of roller-A. When the defect is located near the lower part of roller-B, the constraint reaction force of roller-A reaches the maximum value (978.8 N). This study provides empirical evidence for establishing an online defectdetection AI models. It clarifies the evolution pattern of constraint forces related to crack location. These findings provide data support for developing efficient and accurate defect online detection systems based on AI to address the limitations of traditional methods.

articleTitle: A Novel Scheme for Controlling Intelligent Television by Using Intelligent Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Although the home intelligent camera contains many functions, its application scenarios are still very limited. Based on the widely used big data analysis method and the face recognition function of intelligent camera, this paper designs a novel scheme of using intelligent camera to control intelligent television. The scheme combines intelligent camera, intelligent television, cloud platform and mobile App. The face recognition function of the intelligent camera recognizes people watching intelligent television, and reports to the mobile App remotely through the cloud platform; users can set the duration and period of watching intelligent television through the mobile App, and can also talk with the intelligent camera through the mobile App or send a language prompt message through the mobile App. In addition, the cloud platform can use big data analysis technology to recommend the best intelligent television playback time and duration to the mobile App, so that children can learn and entertain at the same time. The experimental results also show that the scheme has the conditions for popularization. This scheme can effectively realize the control of the intelligent camera on the intelligent television.

articleTitle: Development of Deep Learning-based for Hot-rolled Seamless Steel Pipes' Outer Surface Defect Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Detecting surface defects is crucial during the production process of hot-rolled seamless steel pipes. In order to make up for the shortcomings of traditional inspection methods, this study developed a set of surface defect detection systems of hot-rolled seamless steel pipe by 3D point cloud and deep learning. A 3D point cloud-based defect detection equipment for seamless steel pipe outer surface was developed to achieve full coverage of seamless steel pipe outer surface detection. The defect detection model of seamless steel pipe surface was designed based on the YOLOF algorithm of correcting attention mechanism, and the corresponding software system was developed for online identification. To confirm the efficacy of the proposed approach, the defect pictures collected by a steel pipe factory were used as an implementation case. The experimental results confirm that all types of defects are effectively covered with a detection rate exceeding 99%, while maintaining a false detection rate of under 0.08%. The industrial application shows that compared with the current advanced detection method, the false positive rate of the outer surface is reduced by 9.5% on average. The proposed method has low installation and maintenance costs, which can lay a foundation for further application of seamless steel pipe quality determination, analysis, and control.

articleTitle: High Precision Long Endurance Attitude Algorithm for Marine Control Based on MEMS Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Currently, MEMS-based attitude systems are widely used in the field of UAVs. In the maritime field, most of the attitude systems are based on high-priced gyroscopes such as optical gyroscopes, flexible gyroscopes, etc. Aiming at the problem of attitude accuracy distortion under long- term drift and swing conditions that systems built based on MEMS components face, a high-precision long-endurance attitude algorithm is proposed. This algorithm considers the zero bias and random walk noise of the gyroscope, uses the variance of the measurement residual as a criterion to adaptively compensate for the impact of external acceleration. Combined with the lever arm compensation algorithm to compensate for the impact of rotation angular velocity on the acceleration reference information, it improves Attitude solution accuracy. This article used MEMS inertial elements and the domestically produced ARM building an attitude measurement system to verify the feasibility of the algorithm. The system’s static attitude accuracy, attitude repeatability, dynamic attitude accuracy and attitude accuracy in the eccentric state were verified basing on the turntable. Experimental results show that the static accuracy of the MEMS attitude system based on this algorithm is better than 0.01°, the attitude repeatability is better than 0.015°, and the attitude dynamic accuracy is better than 0.02°. In the case of eccentricity, the attitude accuracy of the system is improved by 3 times compared with before compensation.

articleTitle: An Improved Monocular ORB-SLAM Using Scaled-Invariant Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) is significant in unmanned systems. SLAM algorithms based on stereo cameras and RGB-D cameras have achieved relatively good results. However, monocular SLAM algorithms negatively affect mapping and localization due to the lack of sufficient scale information. In this paper, we employ a new scale-invariant feature to provide better scale invariance and adopt a consistency-based feature point equalization strategy. We conducted experiments on the TUM, EuRoC and KITTI datasets. In conclusion, this algorithm provides a practical and effective solution for feature extracting and matching in computer vision applications.

articleTitle: A Model-Based Approach to Evaluate Electromagnetic Responses in Vehicle Control Systems Influenced by Harness Shielding and Grounding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Modern vehicles are equipped with numerous electrical devices and instruments to function intelligently and facilitate daily life. However, this makes modern vehicles more sensitive to electromagnetic (EM) disturbance, so it is necessary to evaluate EM responses in vehicle control systems during design phases. This paper proposes a model-based approach to evaluate influences of harness shielding and grounding on induced EM responses in vehicle control systems. It takes the control system of a commercial aircraft engine as an example, and constructs the engine control system model integrated from electrical devices and interconnecting multi-branched cable harnesses. The control system is then grounded onto an engine casing serving as the conducting ground, and exposed to EM disturbances generated by plane waves from four directions respectively. Numerical experiment results conclude that: perfect electrical conductor (PEC) shall be used as the conducting ground for vehicle control system EM response evaluation processes; harness shielding may change control system resonant frequencies and shall be equipped for EM response reduction; the grounding of electrical loadings negates the harness shielding effects and amplifies the induced EM responses. These study results provide guidance for designing vehicle control systems immune to EM disturbance who improves the performance reliability of vehicles.

articleTitle: Hot Rolling Finishing Mill Interstand Strip Image Classification Based on Simple Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: The existing strip deviation and control system for finishing rolling stands has achieved automated detection and correction of strip deviation. However, challenges arise in the harsh industrial site environment, including heavy water vapor mist and rack shaking, resulting in low-quality strip images and the potential for missed or incorrect detections. To address these challenges, this paper develops ResNet10 and GoogleNet models based on convolutional neural networks to achieve rapid strip image feature classification. A dataset of strip images collected at the rolling site is established, incorporating grayscale features. Experimental results demonstrate an impressive image classification accuracy of 98.8% and a swift classification time of only 3 ms. This research provides a theoretical foundation and empirical evidence for subsequent image enhancement and edge detection steps.

articleTitle: Simulation and Optimization of the BD1 Pre-rolling Heating Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: The high strength steels need to be heated for a long period in the soaking pit before BD1 billet opening in a steel mill, which greatly decreases the production efficiency. Based on the problem, this work studied the influence of gas supply on the temperature field of mold ingot. The results show that when the gas flow rate is 1, 2 and 4 m/s with the temperature of ingot core being 1255 °C, the furnace time is 24, 17 and 12 h, respectively. Therefore, under the condition of 1 m/s gas supply, the time can reduce 29% when the gas supply is doubled, and the time can reduce 40% when the gas supply is quadrupled.

articleTitle: A Simulation-based Optimization Method for the Number of Toll Lanes of New Toll Stations After Canceling Provincial Toll Station in China
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: This paper focuses on the simulation-based optimization method for the number of toll lanes of new toll stations. Firstly, this paper analyses traffic characteristics of toll station in peak hour. The road users are divided into four categories: ETC (Electronic Toll Collection) passenger cars (with ETC equipment), ETC freight cars, MTC (Manual Toll Collection) passenger cars (without ETC equipment), and MTC freight cars. Then, a VISSIM based Vehicle Traffic and Service Time Simulation Model is calibrated. The input is the service time, and the calibration output is the traffic volume. After the well calibration of the traffic simulation model, the optimized number of ETC lanes and ETC/MTC mixed lanes at the toll station is determined respectively with increasing traffic volume. Finally, numerical results indicate that compared with the traditional method, the optimized number of toll lanes at the exit of the toll station are reduced significantly. It is further validated that this optimized number of toll lanes is also able to ease traffic congestion of the toll stations.

articleTitle: Prediction of Strip Finish Rolling Width Spread Based on Multi-Granularity Cascade Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: The width control accuracy of hot rolling strip is the key to improving product quality, the accurate prediction of finish rolling width spread directly affects the rough rolling width setting model. In order to further improve the accuracy of the finish rolling width spread prediction model, this paper proposes a prediction model based on multi-granularity cascading forest algorithm for hot finish rolling. The collected data were cleaned and normalized, the input features of the model were selected according to the mechanism model and experience, and the model hyperparameters were optimized by grid search and cross-validation, so as to construct the best prediction model. At the same time, support vector machine regression (SVR), decision tree regression (DTR) and random forest regression (RFR) models were used to compare and verify the test data. The experimental results show that 92.643% of the samples have a prediction error of less than 2mm, which has better prediction accuracy than the other models.

articleTitle: A Novel Soft Modeling Framework for Real-time State Prediction in Strip Galvanization Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: In the galvanization process of strip steel, the removal of floating substances formed within the nose end of the furnace is crucial for improving product quality and production efficiency. Due to the complexity of the composition inside the furnace nose and zinc pot, as well as the diverse operating conditions, production personnel find it challenging to predict the state and movement of materials such as strip steel and zinc fluid within the equipment. To overcome these challenges, this study trained the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to predict the zinc fluid state under various operating conditions based on data from finite element simulation. Additionally, digital twin technology is employed to visualize the spatial states of the furnace nose and zinc pot under stable conditions. Experimental results indicate that this system not only accurately predicts the galvanization process of strip steel under different operating conditions but also operates at speeds several hundred times faster than finite element-based simulators. Furthermore, it enables real-time monitoring of the production conditions in the furnace nose and zinc pot areas, providing a basis for operational adjustments of equipment parameters by operators.

articleTitle: Data Analysis of Energy Absorption Behavior of Aluminum Alloy Buffer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Aluminum alloy buffers are widely employed in various engineering applications to absorb impact energy and mitigate potential damage. The design of these buffers, particularly the transitional angle between the pressure head and the aluminum tube, plays a crucial role in their energy absorption performance and load stability. This study investigates the influence of the transitional angle on the energy absorption behavior and crushing force fluctuations through finite element analysis. Eight finite element models were constructed with transitional angles ranging from 14.04° to 30.96°, while other geometric parameters remained constant. Dynamic explicit simulations were performed, and the resulting Mises stress distributions, energy absorption values, and crushing force data were analyzed. The results revealed that the transitional angle had a minimal impact on the stress distribution and maximum Mises stress values, which varied within a narrow range of 197 MPa to 200 MPa across the models. However, the transitional angle significantly affected the energy absorption capacity, with Model-7 (transitional angle of 28.81°) achieving the highest peak value of 3.473 kJ, 1.18 times that of Model-1 (14.04°). Furthermore, the crushing force fluctuations varied substantially among the models, with Model-7 exhibiting the highest variance of 27.31, indicating relatively large fluctuations, while Model-2 (16.70°) had the lowest variance of 2.539, indicating minimal fluctuations. A trade-off between energy absorption performance and load stability was observed, necessitating a balanced design approach based on specific application requirements. The findings provide valuable insights into the role of the transitional angle in optimizing aluminum alloy buffer designs, enabling improved energy absorption and load stability characteristics tailored to specific industrial needs.

articleTitle: Quaternion-Based Finite-Time Attitude Control for Spacecraft Subject to Multiple Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of spacecraft attitude control in finite-time, accounting for constraints on angular velocities and control torques, external disturbances, and an uncertain inertia matrix. Through the utilization of nonlinear transformation technique, the robust control method, the input saturation model, and the backstepping approach, a quaternion-based finite-time attitude control scheme is developed. Extensive analysis is performed to demonstrate that the proposed method achieves near-zero tracking errors within finite time despite the existence of multiple constraints. Ultimately, a numerical example is employed to show the effectiveness of the proposed attitude control scheme.

articleTitle: A Low Complexity Parameter Extraction Digital Predistortion Technique for Frequency Hopping Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: In wireless communication systems, frequency Hooping (FH) is one of the anti-jamming communication systems. However, the nonlinear distortion of power amplifier (PA) in FH communication systems, it will lead to serious signal distortion. This paper proposed a low complexity digital pre-distortion parameter extraction mothed for FH transmitter. The signal's distortion characteristics are integrated into an operator matrix. Consequently, a single set of coefficients is applied to linearize the different carrier frequencies. Finally, the proposed algorithm is experimentally verified. The experimental parameters are set to 20 MHz QAM for the baseband signal and then up-converted to different carriers from 5.6 GHz to 5.7 GHz, with the step of 50MHz.

articleTitle: Planning Research and Simulation Analysis of Distributed Generation in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Reasonable planning in distribution network can effectively improve power distribution, improve node voltage quality and reduce network loss while unreasonable division may also lead to loss increase, node voltage quality decline and other problems. This paper focuses on the site selection and determination of DG, whose main work is a two-stage programming model used to plan the distributed power supply. In the first stage of distributed power planning, the method of calculating the variance index of network active power sensitivity is used to preliminarily determine location and capacity of DG. In the second stage of planning, minimum investment cost and maximum annual income are objective functions. Minimum of voltage deviation and network loss are objective functions of the third stage of planning, in which multi-objective gray Wolf optimization algorithm is used to optimize the distributed power supply. Then apply this model into IEEE33 node system, whose simulation results verify the effectiveness of the established model. At the same time, planning scheme and variation trend of voltage and under different load capacity are discussed.

articleTitle: Research on the Calculation Model of the Influence Function Method for the Complete Roll System of a 20-High Rolling Mill
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: This study presents the development of a novel calculation model for the influence function method, specifically tailored for the complete roll system of a 20-high rolling mill, a critical component in strip shape control. The research incorporates a hybrid approach, leveraging both simply supported beam and cantilever beam models, to accurately determine the elastic bending influence function for the segmented support rolls characteristic of 20-high rolling mills. The proposed method achieves a notable enhancement in calculation precision, with a validated error rate of less than 3% using real-world data from Ansteel’s 20-high rolling mill. This advancement is expected to facilitate the optimization of the rolling process, thereby improving product quality and boosting production efficiency.

articleTitle: Prediction of Head Deviation of Finishing Strip Steel Based on PSO-SVR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: To address the issue of poor accuracy in predicting the head deviation of finishing strip steel, this article describes a prediction model based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Support Vector Regression (SVR) for the head deviation of finishing strip steel. The objective of this model is to improve the prediction accuracy in order to facilitate feedforward control of the head deviation. The control parameters are set from three dimensions: incoming material factors, mill factors, and changes in the rolling process. A dataset of 2000 records from an industrial site is used for training and testing the prediction accuracy. The results demonstrate that the model achieves a high prediction accuracy of 87%. To continue proving the feasibility of the model, the proposed PSO-SVR algorithm is compared with SVR algorithm, polynomial prediction, and extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) prediction. The results show that the PSO-SVR based prediction outperforms other methods. The research provides theoretical and data support for feedforward control of head deviation in the industrial field of strip steel.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic-Mechanical Coupled Winding Vibration Characteristics Analysis of Grounding Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic parameters of the grounding transformer are obtained based on finite element analysis, and then the parameters are substituted into the constructed time-domain equation for electromagnetic-mechanical coupling, and the winding vibration acceleration of the winding and the electromagnetic force are analyzed, and the grounding transformer model is built by COMSOL software for simulation. Because there are few studies on the vibration of the grounding transformer winding in the arc suppression process, it is of great significance to study the vibration analysis of the transformer winding in the arc suppression process.

articleTitle: AI-based Lower Upper Bound Assessing Framework for Predicting Mechanical Properties of Hot-rolled Seamless Steel Pipe
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Mechanical properties are one of the most critical indicators of hot-rolled seamless steel pipe. Seamless steel pipe served in harsh working environments for a long time, putting strict requirements on product quality and mechanical properties. Due to the "data barrier" between each production process's detection and control systems, the process data is impossible to use in predicting and improving product quality. To overcome the above difficulties, this research developed an industrial big data platform to realize a single steel pipe's data interconnection in the hot rolling line. The lower upper bound assesses framework of mechanical properties was established based on quantile regression long short-term memory networks (QRLSTM) model to meet the customer's requirements for the mechanical properties interval of each finished steel pipe. The proposed framework can completely replace manual sampling and inspection at industrial sites, improve production efficiency, and reduce production costs.

articleTitle: Image Restoration of Underwater Bubble Disturbance Based on Improved U-Net Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Distinct from typical underwater imaging, underwater imaging affected by underwater bubble disturbance blurs imaging information, thereby rendering the traditional underwater imaging model no longer being appropriate. We have proposed an improved U-Net network with excellent restoration efficiency and accuracy to weaken the underwater bubble influence. The linear activation function is adopted in our improved U-Net network, and corresponding experimental datasets are captured and processed for further training. Through the underwater restoration experiments, compared with underwater bubble disturbance conditions, our restoration model significantly improves the accuracy of underwater calibration, and subsequently provides a robust guarantee for underwater measurement applications.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of the Impact of Internal Defects on the Mechanical Properties of Solid Axles under Combined Bending and Torsion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: The detection and characterization of internal defects in solid components is crucial for ensuring structural integrity and safety in various engineering applications. This study investigates the influence of internal annular sector-shaped defects on the mechanical behavior of circular solid shafts under combined bending-torsion loading. The research methodology involved developing finite element models with and without internal defects, representing a bending-torsion testing setup. Numerical simulations were performed to analyze the stress distribution, deformation patterns, and reaction forces under various loading conditions. The results revealed that the presence of internal defects significantly alters the stress distribution, leading to localized stress concentrations near the defect location. Furthermore, the maximum Mises stress values were consistently higher in the model with internal defects compared to the defect-free model. The constraint reaction force analysis demonstrated a reduction in mechanical resistance due to internal defects, resulting in lower reaction force values. The main conclusion drawn from this study is that the presence of internal defects has a profound impact on the mechanical behavior of solid shafts under combined bending-torsion loading. The observed variations in stress distribution, maximum Mises stress, and reaction forces offer potential avenues for detecting internal defects based on bending-torsion deformation. These findings contribute to the development of reliable non-destructive testing techniques for ensuring the structural integrity of critical components.

articleTitle: Finite Element Simulation of Hot Rolled Steel Strip Flying Shear Process at High Speed
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: A finite element model was established to simulate the flying shear process of 40Mn strip steel, and the influence of key parameters of the flying shear on the shear was analyzed. Firstly, the kinematic analysis of the flying shear mechanism was carried out to obtain the motion path of the cutting edge in the shearing process. Then, a plane strain finite element model was established on DEFORM software to simulate the flying shear process of 40Mn strip steel. Johnson-Cook plastic constitutive model and damage model considering strain, strain rate hardening and temperature softening were adopted. Through the calculation and analysis of the finite element model, the influence law of the fillet radius of the cutting edge and the relative clearance of the cutting edge on the shearing power and the quality of the cutting section is obtained. Under the given strip size and flying shear conditions, the optimal cutting edge clearance and fillet radius are determined.

articleTitle: Energy Saving Oriented Electricity Load Calculation of High-speed Train Group: A Distributed Computation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Electricity load calculation of high-speed train group is one critical step for traction power system design. The energy-saving oriented electricity load calculation of high-speed train group is time-consuming. A distributed computation framework is proposed to improve the computing efficiency of solution algorithm by splitting the train group into single trains and dividing the railway lines into various sections. The experiment results show that the computing efficiency has been improved by 80.9% and becomes more stable under distributed computation environment.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modelling and Adaptive Control of An Upper-Limb Robotic Exoskeleton
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: This paper presents the modelling and control of a novel upper-limb exoskeleton with a serial structure. The dynamic modelling is performed by using the Newton-Euler method, followed by linear transformations to obtain a minimal parameter set containing unknown dynamic parameters. By considering uncertain factors such as inertial forces and transmission losses within motor internal reducers, a periodic trajectory is designed for the purpose of parameter identification. The weighted least squares method was employed for this purpose, estimated values for the dynamic parameters are calculated and compared with actual values by employing the root mean square error and mean absolute error. Additionally, a zero-force control based on an outer-loop PID strategy has been devised, and the viability of the dynamic model and the controller has been demonstrated through experimentation. The results demonstrate that the proposed upper-limb exoskeleton can be employed to enhance the efficacy of robot-assisted rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Design and Test of Power Chassis for Small Tracked Sand Barrier Placing Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low efficiency of the existing sand barriers burying machinery, large quality of the whole machine, inconvenient operation of large-scale machinery, and difficult to adapt to the complex terrain environment in the desert area, a self-propelled small and flexible power chassis has been developed, which mainly consists of the frame, the power system, the traveling system, and the control system. According to the environment of sand barriers buried, put forward the design target performance requirements and the overall structure of the program; first of all, the walking system components for the calculation and selection, followed by the matching calculation of the drive motor and power battery and the control system hardware circuit design and software programming; finally, the power chassis for the field test. The test results show that the power chassis has good range and climbing ability, with a range of up to 12km, a maximum speed of 6.1km/h, the ability to cross 25° sandy slopes, and a wireless remote control distance of 100m, which is in line with the desert environment driving and sand barriers burying operational needs.

articleTitle: Research on Contact-Type Gravity Field Testing Method for JN-06 Accelerometer Based on Turntable
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Addressing issues such as low testing efficiency, easy introduction of installation errors, and turntable errors in the gravity field testing of the JN-06 quartz flexure accelerometer, a contact-type testing method based on a turntable is proposed. This method utilizes probes to achieve contact connections between the test device and the terminals of the accelerometer, enabling non-destructive and simultaneous testing of multiple accelerometer. Additionally, a reference accelerometer is introduced to ensure consistency between testing conditions and calibration conditions. To verify the feasibility of this method, both contact-type testing experiments and traditional testing experiments were conducted on 11 JN-06D-01 accelerometer. The root mean square errors of zero-bias and scale factor measured by the two experiments are 2.90474E-05 g and 0.00493 P/100s/g respectively. Therefore, the contact-type testing method has higher credibility and verified the feasibility of the testing method.

articleTitle: High Speed Laser Stripe Extraction Method for Measuring Strip Flatness using Linear Structured Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of strip steel flatness calculation, it's hard to overstate the significance of accurately and efficiently extracting the center of laser stripes in strip steel images. It serves as the foundation for accurate calculation of strip steel flatness and adjustment of process parameters. The main intention of this dissertation is to show a solution for efficiently obtaining sub-pixel centerlines of dual line laser stripes, which combines the region of interest (ROI) extraction and the Steger algorithm based on Gaussian operator. The method consists of three steps. Firstly, preprocessing is performed on each laser stripe to remove the background and exclude redundant laser line regions on both sides of the steel plate based on area selection. Secondly, the ROI region is determined using the merging operator, and the processed region is intersected with the pixels of the original image. Finally, according to the pixel width of the stripes, the parameters of the Gaussian operator are calculated, and the center position of the sub-pixel is calculated using Taylor expansion in the normal direction. It has been proven that the processing time for a single dual-line laser image is only 6.779 ms. The most striking conclusion that can be reached when using the indicated method to extract the center position information of laser stripes is quite frankly high precision and efficiency. This method ensures the real-time nature and detection accuracy of industrial steel plate flatness measurement, providing theoretical and data support for process control in industrial settings.

articleTitle: Analysis for influences of eccentric distance on grinding performance of eccentric AG mill using DEM simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Tumbling mill is an industrial equipment for producing fine and uniform granules. In recent decade, the eccentric ball mill is proposed for improving milling efficiency of particles. In this paper, a validated Discrete Element Method (DEM) model is used for simulating charge motion in eccentric AG mill at different eccentric distances ε. The DEM results showed that movement pattern of particles periodically changes as AG mill revolves, when ε is larger than 0·r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>, where r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> is radius of AG mill. Cascading phenomena can be observed in particles in the first half turn of each mill revolution, while most particles roll down from shoulder position in the second half turn. With the increase of ε, the number of high-energy collisions among particles grows dramatically at charge impact point position, while the number of high-energy collisions between particles and lifters is reduced. Based on the DEM results, it can be concluded that the eccentric AG mill can help to improve the grinding efficiency of granular materials while guarantee structural safety of lifters’ boundaries, especially for the large ε.

articleTitle: Method for Live Determination of Caenorhabditis Elegans Based on Deep Learning and Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Caenorhabditis elegans (C.elegans) lifespan monitoring assists compound evaluation scientific research. To address the issues of inaccurate and low to address the issues of inaccurate and low throughput results caused by fatigue in manual identification of C.elegans, a method based on deep learning and image processing is proposed for the identification of C.elegans in industrial camera imaging. This method first manually collects digital images of the whole life cycle of C.elegans, and makes a data set, then trains the best weight file based on YOLOV5; then uses this file for C.elegans target detection; finally, on the basis of the target detection results, the similarity and the intersection over union ratio of the target box binarization are used to determine the target weight of C.elegans. The experimental results show that the YOLOV5 model is superior to the Faster-RCNN and Faster-RCNN_R50 models in C.elegans. R50 models in C.elegans target detection, with an average accuracy of 96.3%, which is about 5% higher than other models. In addition, a visual software is developed according to the proposed model. Compared with manual identification, this method can effectively reduce the identification error of C.elegans individuals and corpses, which are 5.52% and 1.33%, respectively.

articleTitle: A Panoramic Roaming Method of Adaptive Image Content
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Panoramic roaming is based on the real scene view display technology, which can realize fixed-point 360° free roaming. Panoramic roaming is limited by vision, especially expanding Angle, whose stretching deformation will damage scene structure obviously, which is inconformity with the human visual perception. Aiming at the problem of limited view panoramic roaming, based on static panorama accord with human vision, guided by the thought of separation between data processing and image display, the paper constructed a longitudinal layered horizontal block deformation panorama image Pyramid. By the design coded of the panorama image slice adaptive calling and the smooth transition of image and projection model, it achieves the goal which the scene adapts vision during the panoramic roaming.

articleTitle: Nondestructive Detection of Internal Quality of Hami Melon by Hyperspectral Technology Combined with Chemometrics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: In this research, the combination of hyperspectral technology and chemometrics was applied for non-destructive testing of the internal quality of Hami melon. Sugar content and firmness serve as crucial indicators in assessing the internal quality of this fruit. Various pretreatment methods were employed for feature extraction, and subsequently, partial least squares (PLS) prediction models were established for sugar content and firmness. The outcomes reveal that the optimal results for the PLS sugar content prediction model were achieved when utilizing the original spectrum treated with multivariate scattering correction (MSC), resulting in a correlation coefficient of 0.663 and a prediction root-mean-square error of 0.909. Similarly, the PLS firmness prediction model exhibited the best performance when based on the first derivative spectrum treated with the standard normal variable transformation (SNV), yielding a correlation coefficient of 0.674 and a prediction root-mean-square error of 6.388 N. This investigation demonstrates the feasibility of employing hyperspectral technology in combination with chemometrics for simultaneous detection of the internal quality of Hami melon. The findings of this study suggest promising prospects for the future market application of the research method. The integration of hyperspectral technology and chemometrics offers a reliable and efficient approach for non-destructive evaluation of Hami melon quality, paving the way for its potential implementation in the fruit industry to ensure enhanced product quality control and consumer satisfaction.

articleTitle: Data Analysis of Public Opinion Dissemination in Online Emergencies Based on the SEIR Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: The dissemination of online public opinion is influenced by multiple factors, including social network structure, individual behavior, and information dissemination mechanisms, exhibiting characteristics such as suddenness, complexity, and difficulty in containment. The rapid spread of premeditated malicious events can pose a serious threat to social order. This study aims to explore the influencing factors of public opinion dissemination speed in public emergencies. It adopts the SEIR model from the medical field to analyze the evolution of online public opinion during such events. This model categorizes the population into four groups: susceptible, exposed, infected, and recovered, for constructing a simulation model. Through data analysis, we found that effective strategies for responding to and guiding public opinion, as well as controlling the source of online public opinion, can contribute to improving the online public opinion environment. This study offers decision support and serves as a valuable reference for scientifically responding to online public opinion and formulating reasonable strategies.

articleTitle: Multi-Classification Segmentation Method of Gastric Cancer Pathological Images Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Gastric cancer is a serious health threat, and pathological imaging is important in detecting it. These images can assist doctors in accurately determining the location of the cancer, thereby providing an important reference for clinical decision-making. In the field of image processing, deep learning technology is leading to more and more excellent segmentation models. The Trans-Unet model has achieved success in the image segmentation. However, when applying this model to gastric cancer pathological section data, the segmentation boundary appears jagged. We propose three possible solutions. First, we designed an attention connection module to replace the skip connections in the model to enhance the prediction accuracy of the model. Second, we designed a prediction processing unit that takes the model’s prediction results as input and uses a Conditional Random Field (CRF) for further prediction calculations. To enable the model to meet the requirements of multi-classification of images, we designed a dynamic weight selection module to enhance the model’s accuracy for multi-classification tasks. After our optimization, the optimized model improved by 8% on the DSC evaluation index and 39% on the HD evaluation index. In addition, the jagged boundary problem in the prediction results has also been effectively improved. Through comparative experiments and erosion experiments, we found that the improved method enhances the accuracy of model prediction and reduces the jagged results at the boundary.

articleTitle: Quantitative Assessment of Lower-limb Motor Function Based on Multimodal Gait Data for Hip Osteoarthritis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: The Harris Hip Score is very important in the clinical assessment of rehabilitation outcomes following Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA). Harris scales often have issues such as subjectivity and ceiling effects, it is difficult to measure the subtle changes in patients’ disease progression. This paper proposes using deep learning algorithms to process multimodal gait data. First, conducting gait tests on THA patients to obtain optical motion capture data (MOC), surface electromyography data (sEMG), and force platform data (FP). Then, extracting features from these three modalities of data and input them into four models: LSTM, 1DCNN, 1DCNN-LSTM, and LSTM-1DCNN, to get the valuation results. Among these models, the 1DCNN-LSTM model performed best, with an L1Loss value of 9.952 and a correlation coefficient of 0.795 between the predicted values and the actual scores. This indicates that analyzing gait data with the 1DCNN-LSTM network can effectively predict Harris scores, which can provide a fundamental basis for the clinical diagnosis.

articleTitle: Patent Recommendation Methods Based on Transformer Encoders and Regularization Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Patent recommendation service has become a major demand of all walks of life in the society. Patent data collection and analysis can not only help enterprises grasp the development status of the industry, but also provide decision support for them in the research and development process of science and technology services. In view of the problem of inaccurate patent recommendation caused by the inconsistency between the search text and the patent text length and the low accuracy of traditional patent recommendation, a word and sentence dual processing model based on Transformer encoder and regularization strategy is proposed to complete the patent recommendation task from the level of sentence granularity and word granularity. The sentence granularity feature extraction module uses the transformer encoder superimposed multi-head attention method to obtain the feature information between the sentence vector groups, so that the sentence vector fuses the feature information of each sentence, and solves the problem of low recommendation accuracy caused by the inconsistent length of the patent text and the search text; The word granularity feature extraction module uses the twin network model to extract the feature information of the sentence granularity vector using the Transformer encoder using the double splicing operation, improve the model performance and model accuracy; Introduce a strategy based on Dropout and symmetric JS divergence regularization, improve the model generalization ability and accuracy. Experiments have proved that it outperforms SBERT, BERT, MGMSN and SVM models in terms of performance.

articleTitle: Thickness Measurement of Alloy Steel Carburizing Layer Based on Laser Ultrasonic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Carburizing is one of the most widely used chemical heat treatment processes in the machinery manufacturing industry. The surface hardness, wear resistance and flexural fatigue strength of the workpiece after carburization is greatly improved. The thickness of the carburized layer is one of the main technical indicators to measure the quality of carburized parts. However, at present, the carburized shaft carburized layer thickness inspection is generally a contact method. In this paper, the thickness of the carburized layer of alloy steel was detected using Laser Ultrasonic (LU) non-destructive testing technology. First of all, using simulation signals to verify the effectiveness of sparse decomposition reconstruction and wavelet threshold denoising algorithm, and then the use of sparse decomposition and reconstruction combined with wavelet threshold denoising algorithm on the experimental LU signal denoising to extract the weak signal, obtained carburized layer thickness of alloy steel, accuracy of test results up to more than 95%. This study provides theoretical and data support for the development and application of on-line inspection equipment for carburized layers.

articleTitle: A Patent Fast Recommendation Algorithm Based on User Requirements Combined with an Inverted Table
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Patent recommendation has always been an essential service for the innovation and development of all walks of life. The matching of demand and patent information can enable enterprises to quickly obtain the innovation and development trend of the industry. The current patent recommendation method has the problem of slow recommendation speed and insufficient comprehensive recommendation results. According to the existing problems, a patent fast recommendation algorithm based on user needs combined with inverted table is proposed. The algorithm using dual track recommended way for accurate recommendation and extensive recommendation, in the process of recommendation built by patent data inversion table and document list auxiliary recommendation to improve recommendation speed and accuracy, when accurate recommendation when using improved requirements based on GPT-2 compression model recommended after demand text compression, when widely recommended using TF-IDF mechanism for demand text of each paragraph after keyword extraction, finally generate widely recommendation list and accurate recommendation list. This recommendation method can not only realize the fast and accurate recommendation of patents, but also provide users with more innovative ideas for extensive recommendation. The experiments show that the proposed recommendation algorithm has higher speed and accuracy than the original recommendation algorithm.

articleTitle: Monocular Dynamic Object Detection with multi-modal fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: In the field of 3D scene understanding, object motion estimation holds great significance in handling dynamic scenes. To address this, This paper presents a novel method for rigid object motion segmentation from video, integrating multiple data modalities including imagery, optical flow, depth, scene flow, and camera ego-motion. Utilizing a motion filtering module, effectively removes background motion due to camera dynamics, while a motion extraction module accurately segments moving objects. The approach computes the objects’ motion characteristics such as speed, direction, and position using a sophisticated fusion of 3D motion data. Validated on the KITTI dataset, our method demonstrates superior accuracy and robustness in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Optimizing Production through Digitalization: A Case Study on Smart Manufacturing in Port Machinery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: As intelligent manufacturing ushers in Industry 4.0, digital transformation of production facilities is crucial for remaining competitive. This study upgraded a large port machinery equipment workshop through integrating key enabling technologies. Further, A design plan was formulated involving comprehensive surveys and requirements analysis. An intelligent manufacturing workshop was established, comprising automated modules for plate processing, forming, assembly, and logistics. Digital integration between computer-aided design models and virtual manufacturing simulations validated new concepts prior to on-site implementation. Intelligent robot welding stations improved flexibility and reduced cycle times. Economic assessments revealed reductions in production cycle duration, improved material provision timeliness, optimized production rhythms, and lower personnel requirements. Digitalization enabled higher productivity, better resource efficiency, and decreased operating costs. Our study demonstrated how digital transformation enhances production efficiency, quality control, and competitiveness for manufacturing industries.

articleTitle: Classification Method of Hot-Rolled Steel Strip Mechanical Properties Dataset Based on Mechanism and Data Mining to Improve Model Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: Due to the variety of steel grades, predicting and modeling the mechanical properties of hot-rolled steel strips is challenging. Additionally, the limited availability of certain steel grades prevents smooth model construction. Based on clustering algorithms and metallurgical principles, this study proposes an analysis method that combines mechanisms with big data to analyze the correlation between steel grades. This method enables the merging of steel grade samples with similar patterns, providing an effective data processing approach for modeling steel grades with small sample sizes. It considers both data distribution characteristics and internal patterns. Firstly, the dataset undergoes feature transformation based on solid solution and precipitation strengthening. Then, on the basis of normalization, a hierarchical clustering algorithm is employed to categorize the data, aggregating data with similar distribution characteristics. Subsequently, the t-SNE algorithm and polynomial regression assess cluster internal consistency, facilitating merging of similar clusters. Finally, mechanical property prediction models are constructed for each cluster to validate the method’s effectiveness. The results indicate that after dividing the dataset according to the proposed method, the prediction accuracies of yield strength, tensile strength, and elongation have increased by 2.31%, 1.32%, and 2.28% respectively. This has certain reference value for the industrial application of mechanical property prediction technology.

articleTitle: Simulation Calculation of Energy Load at Railway Stations Based on Dynamic Passenger Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: This article consider dynamic changes in passenger flow, focuses on the energy consumption calculation of high-speed railway passenger stations, starting from the aspects of station ventilation and air conditioning, escalators, lighting, and electrical equipment. Based on the dynamic passenger flow in the waiting room, a refined calculation of the energy consumption of high-speed railway passenger stations throughout the day is carried out. The analysis and calculation method is used to evaluate various loads in different time periods, taking Changsha South Station as an Example and then evaluate the energy consumption of the main body of the station.

articleTitle: MyoLite: Compressible Neural Networks Based on Biokinematics and Self-attention for Fingers Motion Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: With more attention drawn to brain-machine interface (BCI) technology, sEMG-based human-machine interaction (HMI) is used more often in virtual reality (VR), prostheses, exoskeletons, robots, and medical rehabilitation. However, users are no longer satisfied with the recognition of a few discrete gestures, but tend to vividly and continuously track the finger movements for getting better interaction experience. In this paper, with a sparse sEMG armband, we propose a compressible neural network, MyoLite, which is an explainable end-to-end network model including electrode decomposition, myo encoding and myo decoding, to achieve continuous motion tracking of fingers by bioanatomical analysis. Besides, we analysed the linkage relationship of finger movements through self-attention mechanism to compress and generalize the network model. With a public dataset, MyoLite obtains a higher accuracy of finger joint motion tracking than previous methods. The results show the root-mean-square error (RMSE) reaches to 6.10° and the fit is approaching 90.93%. Furthermore, while maintaining the accuracy, the bionic analysis-based compression strategy achieves 30% reduction in the amount of weighting parameters and 31.9% reduction in the floating-point operations per second (FLOPs).

articleTitle: Multi-LiDAR-Inertial Odometry Combined with Vehicle Kinematics for Autonomous Buses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: The application of multi-LiDAR setup in autonomous buses is becoming increasingly widespread. However, challenges in real-world applications of multi-LiDAR SLAM remain largely unexplored. This paper introduces a multi-LiDAR-inertial odometry algorithm that utilizes vehicle kinematics to improve positioning accuracy and reliability. First, we introduce a sensor fusion method that synchronizes and integrates data from point cloud, IMU, and wheel encoder in the shortest possible time intervals, using IMU data to correct point cloud distortions. Subsequently, we developed a multi-sensor fusion odometry system combining multi-LiDAR, IMU, and vehicle wheel encoder data. Finally, leveraging the odometry’s results, we generated a comprehensive global point cloud map. The evaluation of the proposed method in real-world scenarios demonstrates its capability to achieve high-precision odometry data and state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: A Novel Adaptive Deep Belief Network for Bearing Fault Diagnosis in Variable Working Conditions Based on Salp Swarm Algorithm Under Small Sample
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: The actual operating conditions of equipment are complicated and changeable, and it is not easy to obtain enough training sample data quickly. Meanwhile, setting neural network structure parameters by experience or repeated trials will also affect the diagnosis results. To solve this issue, a Domain Adaptive Deep Belief Network based on SSA and Second-Order Statistics Transfer (SSA-SOST-DADBN) of features is proposed. Firstly, the structure parameters of deep belief network (DBN) were optimized by salp swarm algorithm. By solving the envelope spectrum of bearing signal, the hidden information of fault characteristic frequency is obtained, and the training dataset of DBN is constructed. The covariance matrix of distribution of features across the different domains is considered to realize transfer training under different operating situations. The dropout method is employed for effective small-sample rolling bearing fault diagnosis so as to mitigate the risk of overfitting in the network. Based on the public dataset of CWRU, the experiment proves that the network has high accuracy. The method can achieve an average classification accuracy as 95.08% under different working conditions, which has higher accuracy and generalization compared with the other 5 methods.

articleTitle: A Novel Strategy of Additional Tension Optimization for Strip Tandem Cold Rolling Enabled by Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Information, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics and Automation (AIMERA)
abstract: During the speed increase rolling process of tandem cold rolling, applying precise additional tension can effectively suppress rolling force fluctuations, thereby improving the shape of the strip head and reducing thickness fluctuations, ultimately improving the quality of the strip. In order to solve the problem of low accuracy in applying additional tension through manual experience in industrial sites, which leads to excessive fluctuations in rolling force, this paper first proposes an additional tension compensation model, and then conducts theoretical calculations using the improved Multi Group Differential Evolution Particle Swarm Optimization (Imp-PSODE) algorithm. The results show that the optimized additional tension value of the algorithm can accurately reduce rolling force deviation. Industrial practice has shown that compared with the original method, this research can effectively improve the phenomenon of large head shape quality and thickness deviation.
